assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.3 [3327,3605) and [7115,8127) connect the notice definition to the publication conditions and placement rules. The Opaque-copy paragraph begins immediately after the second interval with its own conditions.

challenge.method: Tested exactly 100, then 101 qualifying copies with and without required texts. Compared a Transparent copy on qualifying media with an Opaque copy on media outside the cover trigger.
challenge.results: Exactly 100 and a notice requiring no texts each defeat the cover trigger. At 101, qualifying printed or customarily covered media can trigger it even for Transparent copies. Conversely, publishing or distributing more than 100 Opaque copies can trigger the separate Transparent-copy or network route without either the cover-medium condition or required texts. Both duties can also apply together.

limitations: A particular work’s notice, its authorized edition and the character of the medium require independent evidence. The clause also governs publisher identification and front-cover title presentation.
reasoning: GNU 1.3 §3 requires the designated front and back passages on their corresponding covers when the publisher issues more than 100 printed copies or copies on media commonly carrying printed covers and the work’s notice requires the passages. If legibility would suffer, the publisher should keep the earliest listed texts that reasonably fit on the affected cover and continue the rest on adjacent pages.
